source.title: Learn with Noisy Data via Unsupervised Loss Correction for Weakly Supervised Reading Comprehension
source.authors: Xuemiao Zhang; Kun Zhou; Sirui Wang; Fu-Zheng Zhang; Zhong-Yuan Wang; Junfei Liu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies varying amounts of synthetic answer-span noise in weakly supervised reading comprehension and reports model performance, extending noisy-label findings to a different task and data modality.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-set EM and F1 under synthetic noise ratios, including original-loss baselines. It does not report training error for these runs. Cited image-classification noise work and its results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study extends label-noise experiments to reading comprehension. Original-loss baselines measure the held-out degradation component of V4, and Section 2.2 reports early training-loss differences relevant to V6. Neither establishes eventual memorization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report larger early losses for noisy samples and conclude that hierarchical loss correction using a fitted GMM and hard bootstrapping improves weakly supervised MRC performance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses weakly supervised MRC with synthetic answer-span corruption and natural distantly supervised data. It studies loss correction rather than fitting fully random image labels; the reported metrics are held-out EM and F1.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with noise ratio, model, and loss-correction strategy.

fits_no_version.finding: GMM noise-identification accuracies in Table 2 measure detection performance, rather than random-label fitting or temporal memorization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss distributions can help identify corrupted answer-span supervision.

fits_no_version.finding: Held-out improvements from loss correction and comparisons of GMM with BMM measure mitigation performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reweighting losses and modifying the training objective can improve reading comprehension trained with noisy supervision.

record.problems: The reported results are evaluation EM and F1, not training error. The synthetic SQuAD corruption replaces answer spans with random continuous token sequences, rather than assigning completely random labels to all training examples. No uncertainty estimates are reported in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were extracted. Table 1 reports held-out task scores under answer-span corruption, but those scores do not establish the V4 training-fit and chance-test-error outcomes. The flattened table layout also makes it difficult to associate every displayed score with a model and method without ambiguity.

untested.parts: No fully randomized training set, near-zero training-error result, or chance-level test comparison.
No training-time ratio or quantified convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
No experiments with shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit, memorization of corrupted labels, and approach to a measured chance baseline are untested; corruption stops at 80%.
No relevant comparison of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation.
No demonstrated transition from learning shared patterns to memorizing noise, or eventual successful fitting of noisy labels.

missing.what: The qualitative early training-loss comparison: noisy samples have larger early losses than clean samples under the original objective. Record the clean-versus-80%-corrupted SQuAD convergence comparison without inventing numerical values or identifying an unspecified model.
missing.locator: Section 2.2 and Figure 1(a), page 2626; reiterated in the abstract and conclusion.

record.verdict_notes: The record overlooks V6 evidence. Its V4 verdict is defensible only for held-out degradation, not perfect training fit or noise memorization. Its reference to R1–R24 is invalid because no rows were extracted. The supplied text contains Figure 1's caption and interpretation, but no readable plotted values.

versions.untested_parts: Does not assign completely random labels to the entire training set, report training error on such a set, or report test error at chance.
Does not compare training time or convergence speed for true versus random labels or across corruption fractions.
Does not train on shuffled pixels, permuted inputs, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Reports held-out EM and F1 under different synthetic answer-span noise ratios, but does not report perfect training fit, test error approaching chance, or whether the models capture remaining signal while memorizing noise.
Does not test weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation against random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Does not compare when real versus noisy or random labels are learned during training.

relationships.condition: Original cross-entropy baselines for BiDAFm, BiDAF, and BERT on SQuAD with 0–80% answer-span corruption; held-out degradation component only.
relationships.reason: Table 1 shows monotonically declining EM and F1 for all three baselines. From clean to 80% corruption, EM falls from 60.19 to 5.07, 64.18 to 10.35, and 69.56 to 15.49, respectively. Based on text/table evidence; no rows exist, and rows_left_out explicitly declares this omission.
relationships.display_finding: EM and F1 declined monotonically for all three baselines, with EM falling from 60.19 to 5.07 for BiDAFm, 64.18 to 10.35 for BiDAF, and 69.56 to 15.49 for BERT.

relationships.condition: Early training under original cross-entropy loss in weakly supervised MRC; learning differences only.
relationships.reason: Section 2.2 explicitly reports larger early losses for noisy samples than clean samples, consistent with preferential early learning of clean supervision. Figure 1(a) compares clean SQuAD and 80%-corrupted SQuAD convergence. Based on text; the relevant result is missing from the record.
relationships.display_finding: Noisy samples had larger early losses than clean samples, with convergence also compared between clean SQuAD and SQuAD with 80% corruption.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
